from.place: Paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient-adjunction and inverse-limit calculation, and the following naturality and triangle-identity sentences; foundational enhancement of finite coefficient adjunction diagrams. Technical input: Pinched simplices give a weakly equivalent mapping resolution. Smaller input: Cone straightening sends right anodyne maps to equivalences and recovers fibers. Item proof: contravariant model category and fiberwise detection used in Steps 2 and 6.

title: The contravariant simplicial model structure over an arbitrary simplicial set
statement:
Use simplicial sets, horns, geometric realization and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], right fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], right anodyne maps of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne], the coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], and the model-category conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Fix a small simplicial set $S$, in a universe enlarged when necessary. The category $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$ has objects maps to $S$ and morphisms commuting with those maps. Here cofibrantly generated means that there are small sets $I,J$ of morphisms such that trivial fibrations are exactly the $I$-injective maps, fibrations are exactly the $J$-injective maps, and every map admits functorial factorizations as an $I$-cell map followed by an $I$-injective map and as a $J$-cell map followed by a $J$-injective map. A $K$-injective map has the right lifting property against every member of $K$; a $K$-cell map is a transfinite composite, continuous at limit stages, of pushouts of coproducts of members of $K$. For $a:X\to S$ put $C^\triangleright(a)=S\amalg_X(X\star\Delta^0)$, where the join has degree-$r$ simplices $X_r\amalg\{v_r\}\amalg\coprod_{0\leq u<r}X_u$, with the first $u+1$ vertices in $X$ and the remaining vertices at $v$. For a small simplicial category $A$, let $\pi_0A$ have the same objects and morphisms the path components of the realizations of its mapping simplicial sets, with induced composition. Call a simplicial map $u:U\to V$ a categorical equivalence if $\mathfrak C[u]:\mathfrak C[U]\to\mathfrak C[V]$ induces weak homotopy equivalences on all mapping simplicial sets and an equivalence of the categories $\pi_0\mathfrak C[U]\to\pi_0\mathfrak C[V]$.

There is a cofibrantly generated model structure on $\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$, with functorial factorizations, whose cofibrations are degreewise injections, whose weak equivalences $f:(X,a)\to(Y,b)$ are exactly the maps for which $C^\triangleright(a)\to C^\triangleright(b)$ is a categorical equivalence, and whose fibrations have the right lifting property against cofibrations which are weak equivalences. Every right anodyne map over $S$ is a trivial cofibration. Its fibrant objects are exactly the right fibrations $X\to S$. Their strict vertex fibers $X_s=X\times_S\{s\}$ are Kan complexes. A map $f:X\to Y$ between right fibrations over $S$ is a weak equivalence in this model structure if and only if $f_s:X_s\to Y_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every vertex $s$. No quasicategory hypothesis on $S$ is required.

source.place: Definition 1.1.5.14 and Remark 1.1.5.17 (categorical equivalences via coherent realization); Definition 2.1.4.5 and Propositions 2.1.4.7-2.1.4.9, dualized as in Remark 2.1.4.12; Corollaries 2.2.3.12-2.2.3.13; Kan fibers also follow from Lemma 2.1.3.3. No Stacks tag states this contravariant simplicial model structure.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=\mathrm{sSet}_{/S}$. For the small category $\Delta/S$ of simplices $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$ and their commuting simplex maps, an object $X\to S$ corresponds to the presheaf assigning to $\sigma$ the fiber of $X_n\to S_n$ at $\sigma$. Conversely take $X_n=\coprod_{\sigma\in S_n}F(\sigma)$, with operators induced by those of $F$. These constructions are inverse, including on maps. Thus [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] makes $\mathcal A$ locally presentable. Limits are compatible tuples of elements in each such fiber, and colimits are disjoint unions modulo the diagram relations, so $\mathcal A$ is complete and cocomplete. Let $I_S$ contain every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ equipped with each possible map $\Delta^n\to S$, for $n\geq0$. This is a small set. By [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], each monomorphism is obtained by adjoining its missing nondegenerate simplices along their boundaries; equip each attachment with its map into $S$. Hence the weakly saturated closure of $I_S$ is exactly the degreewise injections. Pushouts, composites and retracts preserve degreewise injectivity, as is seen in each set of simplices.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7, condition (2); ordinary category-of-elements description of the slice.

proof.text: For a right fibration $E\to S$, pullback along a vertex $s$ is still a right fibration: a lifting square in the pullback projects to one for $E\to S$, and the filler has the prescribed base simplex, so lies in the pullback. Apply [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] with base $\Delta^0$ to obtain that $E_s$ is Kan, including its missing-index-zero horns. More generally write $M_S(A,E)=\operatorname{Fun}_{/S}(A,E)$. The horn lifting problem for $M_S(A,E)\to\Delta^0$ at a positive-index horn is the problem of extending a map to $E$ from $A\times\Lambda_i^n$ to $A\times\Delta^n$ over the fixed map to $S$. The product lemma [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], with the monomorphism $\varnothing\to A$, makes this inclusion right anodyne. Right-fibration lifting extends from horns to their saturation: fill a pushout by its attaching square, fill successive stages by transfinite recursion and take the compatible colimit map at limits, and restrict a filler along an arrow retract. Thus $M_S(A,E)$ is a right fibration over a point and is Kan by [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber]. If $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ is any monomorphism over $S$, a positive-index horn lifting problem for restriction $M_S(B,E)\to M_S(A,E)$ adjoints to extension from $(B\times\Lambda_i^n)\cup(A\times\Delta^n)$; the same product lemma makes this right anodyne. Restriction is therefore a right fibration with Kan base $M_S(A,E)$, so [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] makes it a Kan fibration.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.3.3 and Lemma 2.2.3.4; right-anodyne pushout-product lifting; use a point as base only after taking the indicated pullback or slice mapping object.

proof.text: Define $W_S$ by the coherent right-cone condition. For a right horn $j:\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with $0<i\leq n$, the relative cone map is a pushout of $\Lambda_i^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$: the horn contains the entire initial face $\Delta^n$ opposite the new last vertex, which is attached to $S$, and its other faces are precisely the cones on the faces of $\Lambda_i^n$. The index $i$ is inner since $0<i<n+1$. This is a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-coherent-inner-anodyne-equivalences]. The same assertion holds for every right anodyne $j$. Indeed adjoining the right cone, with its apex fixed, preserves pushout squares and continuous transfinite chains; check this degreewise from the pure and mixed summands of the cone. Thus the relative cone map for a pushout or transfinite composite of horns is a pushout or composite of the indicated inner-anodyne maps. Arrow retract diagrams also pass through the cone functor. The inner-anodyne class is closed under exactly these operations. Apply the cited coherent-realization assertion again. Right anodyne maps are monic, since their horn generators are monic and these operations preserve injections degreewise. We also record that for every $A\to S$, $A\times\{1\}\hookrightarrow A\times\Delta^1$ is right anodyne: use [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product] on the right horn $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow A$.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.4.6, dualized: direct relative-cone inner-horn calculation, and Corollary 2.1.2.7.

proof.text: An $I_S$-injective $p:X\to Y$ has every underlying boundary lift, since the bottom simplex in $Y$ determines its map to $S$. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] it is a trivial Kan fibration. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms], choose a section $t:Y\to X$ and a homotopy $H:X\times\Delta^1\to X$ over $Y$ from $tp$ to $1_X$: lift respectively $\varnothing\hookrightarrow Y$ and $X\times\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow X\times\Delta^1$ with base map $p\operatorname{pr}_X$. Put $P=X\times\Delta^1\to S$. Its endpoint $e_1:X\to P$ belongs to $W_S$ by Step 3. The projection $r:P\to X$ is in $W_S$ by two-out-of-three, since $re_1=1_X$. The other endpoint $e_0$ is then in $W_S$ since $re_0=1_X$. Likewise $H\in W_S$ since $He_1=1_X$, and hence $tp=He_0\in W_S$. To conclude $p\in W_S$, no general localization-saturation theorem is needed. The coherent realizations of $C_S(X)$ and $C_S(Y)$ both have object set $S_0\amalg\{v\}$, and all induced cone functors fix it. Since $pt=1_Y$, on every ordered pair of objects the mapping-set map induced by $p$ is an arrow retract of the mapping-set map induced by $tp$, using the identity on its source and the mapping-set maps of $t,p$ on its target. The latter is a weak homotopy equivalence because $tp\in W_S$; retract closure in the Kan model makes the former a weak homotopy equivalence. The cone functor is the identity on objects, so it is also essentially surjective on components. It is therefore a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, proving $p\in W_S$. This is the direct section-and-cylinder argument in HTT condition (3), with no right-fibration mapping criterion.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7, condition (3), dualized: section and explicit cylinder endpoints.

proof.text: The statement [lem-coef-cone-equivalence-saturation] supplies isomorphisms, two-out-of-three, filtered-colimit closure, a small filtered-colimit generating family for $W_S$, and pushout stability along the monomorphisms. Step 1 supplies the complete, cocomplete locally presentable category and the small generating set $I_S$ for its cofibrations; Step 4 supplies $I_S$-injectives in $W_S$. Apply [lem-coef-perfect-weak-equivalence-model-recognition] with these data. It gives a model structure with precisely the required cofibrations and cone weak equivalences, fibrations exactly the right lifting class of their intersection, and two small generating sets for its functorial weak factorization systems. Since Step 3 made every right anodyne map both monic and in $W_S$, those maps are trivial cofibrations in this model structure.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4.7, application of Proposition A.2.6.15; Remark 2.1.4.12.

proof.text: To obtain exactly the cell factorizations requested in the statement, choose small generating sets $I,J$ for the two weak factorization systems in Step 5. Their maps are cofibrations, hence degreewise injections. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to all simplices of all their domains, together with a countable set, to choose an infinite regular $\kappa$ larger than their total cardinality. A map from any such domain into the colimit of a continuous $\kappa$-chain of cell attachments factors through a stage: choose a stage for each of its fewer than $\kappa$ simplices and bound those stages by regularity. All stages embed degreewise in their colimit, so the simplex relations already hold at that stage, and two such maps become equal at a common later stage. The same argument applies over $S$. These are exactly the smallness hypotheses of [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization]. Apply it separately to $I,J$. The resulting functorial factorizations have $I$-cell and $J$-cell first maps and their respective injective second maps; the injective classes are respectively the trivial fibrations and fibrations by the chosen generating sets. All indexing sets and ordinals are small in the chosen universe.

source.place: Small-object cell factorization underlying Proposition A.2.6.15; the cardinal bound is written explicitly for simplicial domains.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction] to the raw ordered-cone adjunction $L_S\dashv U_S$. If $F$ is projectively fibrant and $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ is a trivial cofibration in the model constructed in Step 5, then $L_S(j)$ is a projective cofibration and an objectwise weak equivalence. It is therefore a projective trivial cofibration. By projective fibrancy every map $L_S(A)\to F$ extends across $L_S(j)$. Ordinary adjunction identifies this extension exactly with an extension $B\to U_S(F)$ of the original $A\to U_S(F)$ over $S$. Thus $U_S(F)$ is fibrant in the model already constructed; this argument uses neither a Quillen-equivalence theorem nor any identification of all right fibrations with fibrant objects. Conversely every fibrant object is a right fibration because the right horns are trivial cofibrations by Step 3.

source.place: Construction of Section 2.2.1; preservation portion of Theorem 2.2.1.2; Proposition 2.1.4.9(3).

proof.text: Let $E\to S$ be a right fibration. The equivalence of simplicial categories [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent] gives a projectively bifibrant $F$, maps $e:E\to U_S(F)$ and $r:U_S(F)\to E$ over $S$, and a simplicial homotopy $h:E\times\Delta^1\to E$ from $1_E$ to $re$. The specified orientation can also be obtained by reversing an edge in the Kan mapping space of Step 2. Set $Y=U_S(F)$, which is fibrant by Step 7. Given a trivial cofibration $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ and a map $a:A\to E$ over $S$, extend $ea$ to $b:B\to Y$ by fibrancy of $Y$. On $(A\times\Delta^1)\cup(B\times\{1\})$ define a map to $E$ by $h(a(-),-)$ on the first part and $rb$ on the second. They agree on $A\times\{1\}$, since $rbj=rea$. The inclusion of this union into $B\times\Delta^1$ is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied to $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and the monomorphism $j$. Lift against $E\to S$. Restricting the extension to $B\times\{0\}$ gives a map extending $a$. Hence $E$ is fibrant. This proves both fibrancy implications; Step 2 gives the Kan fiber clause. The straightening input is HTT Proposition 2.2.3.11, proved by the simplex comparison of Lemmas 2.2.3.7, 2.2.3.9--10 and descent, rather than the downstream theorem which cites this item.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.12: explicit homotopy-extension proof following Proposition 2.2.3.11.

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a cone weak equivalence between right fibrations. They are cofibrant (all initial maps are monic) and fibrant by Step 8. For each $A=X,Y$, the maps $A\amalg A\hookrightarrow A\times\Delta^1\to A$ are a good cylinder: the first is monic, and the second is a weak equivalence since its terminal-vertex section is right anodyne by Step 3. Apply [lem-coef-model-cylinder-whitehead] with precisely these two cylinders. It yields $g:Y\to X$ and homotopies over $S$ from $gf$ to $1_X$ and from $fg$ to $1_Y$. Restricting their domains and codomains to the strict fiber over any vertex $s$ preserves these products with $\Delta^1$, because the homotopies are over the fixed projection to $S$. Thus $f_s$ has a simplicial homotopy inverse. By [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], $f_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This implication uses no converse cone/mapping criterion.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.13; ordinary model Whitehead with specified product cylinders.

proof.text: Conversely suppose every $f_s$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Let $P_S(Y)$ have $n$-simplices maps $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to Y$ whose projection to $S$ is constant in the interval coordinate. Define $M=X\times_{Y,\operatorname{ev}_0}P_S(Y)$ and $q:M\to Y$ by $\operatorname{ev}_1$. We verify $q$ is a right fibration. For a right horn lifting square against $q$, first extend the given horn into $X$ using $X\to S$ over the simplex of $S$ prescribed by the bottom simplex in $Y$. The desired map into $Y$ is now fixed on $(\Lambda_i^n\times\Delta^1)\cup(\Delta^n\times\partial\Delta^1)$: it is the given path on the horn, $f$ of the chosen $X$-extension at $0$, and the bottom simplex at $1$. These maps agree on intersections. The inclusion of that union is right anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-right-anodyne-product], applied to the right horn and the monomorphism $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. Lifting against $Y\to S$ supplies the path extension, which together with the chosen $X$-extension is the required lift into $M$. For a vertex $y\in Y_s$, the strict fiber $M_y$ is exactly the mapping-path homotopy fiber of $f_s:X_s\to Y_s$: all its simplices have constant base $s$. By Step 2 these are maps of Kan complexes. [lem-coef-space-path-fibration-replacement] makes the path-replacement map a Kan fibration. Its strict fiber is Kan: project any horn to the constant simplex at $y$ and use that fibration to fill it in the same fiber. Thus $M_y$ is Kan, and [lem-coef-space-contractible-fiber-equivalence] makes it weakly contractible. Apply [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] to the right fibration $q:M\to Y$ to conclude that $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration. That result allows an arbitrary simplicial base $Y$, as required here.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.6, mapping-path proof of the fiberwise Whitehead implication; right horn prism product and contractible-fiber criterion are the independent inputs.

proof.text: Keep $M$, $q$ from Step 10, and let $r:M\to X$ be projection and $j:X\to M$ the constant-path inclusion. Then $rj=1_X$ and $qj=f$. There is an explicit simplicial homotopy $H:M\times\Delta^1\to M$ over $S$ from $jr$ to $1_M$: on a pair $(x,\gamma)$ and interval parameter $u$, keep $x$ and replace its path by $t\mapsto\gamma(\min(t,u))$. Here $\min:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ is the nerve of the order-preserving minimum map $[1]\times[1]\to[1]$; this formula therefore defines a simplicial map. At $t=0$ the new path still starts at $f(x)$, and its projection to $S$ is unchanged, so the formula lands in $M$. At $u=0$ it is the constant path at $f(x)$, giving $jr$, and at $u=1$ it is the original path. For $P=M\times\Delta^1$, its terminal section $e_1:M\to P$ belongs to $W_S$ by Step 3. Two-out-of-three in [lem-coef-cone-equivalence-saturation], applied to $\operatorname{pr}_M e_1=1_M$ and $\operatorname{pr}_M e_0=1_M$, puts the projection and $e_0$ in $W_S$. Since $He_1=1_M$, it also puts $H$ and $jr=He_0$ in $W_S$. For every ordered pair of objects of the coherent cones, the mapping-simplicial-set arrow induced by $j$ is an arrow retract of the one induced by $jr$: the map of sources into that retract diagram is induced by $j$, its retraction by $r$, and both maps of targets are the identity. The commutativities are $(jr)j=j$ and $jr=jr$, and the retraction equality is $rj=1_X$. Retract closure of weak homotopy equivalences in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes each mapping-set map of $j$ a weak equivalence. These cone functors fix the common object set $S_0\amalg\{v\}$, so $j$ is a cone weak equivalence. Finally $q$ is a trivial Kan fibration by Step 10, hence is $I_S$-injective and lies in $W_S$ by Step 4. Thus $f=qj$ lies in $W_S$. Together with Step 9 this proves both directions of fiberwise detection over arbitrary small $S$, without a quasicategory assumption.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.3.13, converse; explicit mapping-path contraction written by the second reader, followed by the section/retract argument of Proposition 2.1.4.7(3). No mapping-test criterion is used.
